primary_outcome_name: Sunnybrook Facial Grading System (SFGS) total composite score (comprising resting symmetry, voluntary movement, and synkinesis subscales)
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: SFGS total composite score, 0-100 (0 = total paralysis, 100 = normal facial function)
primary_timepoint: Change score from baseline to 20th day (post-intervention, end of 3-week treatment); assessments also taken at baseline and 10th day (mid-intervention)
population_detail: Adults with acute, primary unilateral idiopathic lower motor neuron facial palsy (Bell's palsy), hospital-based recruitment (Kasturba Medical College, Mangalore, India), enrolled Feb 2020-Mar 2021

published_estimate.quote: Abstract: 'Change scores revealed greater improvement in the SFGS score (p = 0.002) for the experimental group participants.' (Abstract, p. 1). This corresponds to Table 3, row 'SFGS-total composite score', 'Baseline to 20th day': 'Experimental Group [Median (IQR)] 59.0 (42.5-63.0) ... Conventional Group [Median (IQR)] 24.0 (9.0-32.0) ... p-value 0.002*' (Table 3, 'Comparison of change scores across the groups (n = 23)', p. 5). No mean difference, CI, or SE is reported anywhere for this contrast; only group medians/IQRs and the Mann-Whitney U p-value are given.

B_covariate_list: none used in the primary effect analysis; Age (and gender) were compared only as a baseline-balance/randomization check (Table 1, e.g. Age p = 0.74) and were never entered as a covariate/adjustment variable in any outcome comparison
registration_id: CTRI/2020/02/023240 (paper text renders it as 'CTRI/2020/02/023,240'; the comma is very likely a PDF text-extraction artifact, not part of the actual registry ID)
data_availability_statement: Data sheet and appendix are available from https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/UVW89.

registry_check.issues: 1) OUTCOME VARIABLE: The paper's headline/primary result (quoted in the Abstract and matching Table 3 exactly, p = 0.002) is for the SFGS TOTAL COMPOSITE SCORE, baseline-to-20th-day change score - not the voluntary movement (VM) subscore alone. Our registry's outcome_var=VM2 is mismatched on two counts: (a) it targets the VM subscore rather than the composite score the paper's abstract/headline result refers to (the VM subscore's own baseline-to-20th-day change-score p-value in Table 3 is p = 0.013, not p = 0.002); (b) inspection of the deposited 'Data sheet.xlsx' shows VM1/VM2/VM3 correspond to baseline/10th day (mid-intervention)/20th day (post-intervention) respectively - so VM2 is the MID-intervention value, not the final (20th-day) follow-up value used in the paper's primary change-score analysis (which would require VM3). 2) COMPOSITE SCORE AVAILABILITY: Contrary to our prior note ('SFGS-Composite nicht im Datensatz'), the deposited Data sheet.xlsx DOES contain the SFGS total composite score, as columns T1 (baseline)/T2 (10th day)/T3 (20th day) - verified by recomputing group medians from the raw data, which reproduce the published Table 1/Table 2 composite-score medians exactly (e.g., experimental baseline median 31.5, 20th-day median 90.0). So a composite-score re-analysis is in fact possible from the deposited data; the registry should reference T1 (baseline) vs T3 (20th day/final), not VM1/VM2. 3) CONTROL ARM: Cross-checking the deposited dataset's Group/Age/Gender columns against Table 1 shows Group=1 reproduces the EXPERIMENTAL group's reported baseline statistics exactly (median age 39.5 vs Table 1's 39.5; 58.3% male vs Table 1's 58.3%) and Group=2 reproduces the CONVENTIONAL/control group's statistics exactly (median age 45.0; 90.9% male); Group=2 is also the arm containing the single participant lost to follow-up, consistent with the paper's text ('Following allocation to the conventional group... data collection for one patient was incomplete and lost to follow-up'). This means Group=1 = experimental/intervention arm and Group=2 = conventional/control arm - the OPPOSITE of our registry's arm_control=1. 4) COVARIATE: covars_published=Age in our registry does not correspond to an actual adjustment covariate in the paper; Age was used only for a baseline-balance test (Table 1), not in any outcome model (the primary analysis is an unadjusted nonparametric group comparison of change scores).

analysis_method_quote: Statistical analysis: 'Data analysis was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 25.0. Demographic and clinical characteristics at baseline were compared between treatment groups to assess the effectiveness of the randomization procedure. Results were presented as proportions and summary measures. Group comparisons utilized the Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon's signed-rank, and Mann-Whitney U tests. Analyses of outcome data were performed by an experienced statistician blinded to group allocation. A p-value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.' (Methods, 'Statistical analysis', p. 2-3)
notes: Declaration ambiguity: Methods/'Outcome measures' explicitly states 'The primary outcome measure was the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System (SFGS)...The total SFGS composite score ranges between 0 and 100' (p. 3), immediately foregrounding the composite score. The Abstract, however, states 'Primary outcomes were facial symmetry and voluntary movement; assessed by the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System (SFGS)' (p. 1), naming only two of the three SFGS subdomains (excluding synkinesis) and not explicitly naming the composite. Despite this wording, the Abstract's own quantitative headline claim ('Change scores revealed greater improvement in the SFGS score (p = 0.002)') numerically matches ONLY the total-composite-score row of Table 3 (baseline-to-20th-day, p = 0.002), not the voluntary-movement row (p = 0.013) or the resting-asymmetry row (p = 0.001) - so the composite score is what the authors effectively treat as their headline/primary result, and it is coded here as the primary outcome accordingly. All candidate outcomes considered: SFGS resting asymmetry, SFGS voluntary movement, SFGS total composite score (chosen), FDI physical function, FDI social function, House-Brackmann Scale - listed for transparency since the declaration is not fully unambiguous. No mean/SD is reported anywhere in the paper for any SFGS or FDI outcome; all group summaries use Median (IQR) with nonparametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis / Wilcoxon signed-rank / Mann-Whitney U), consistent with the small per-arm sample size (n=12/11). Analysis is unadjusted (no covariates, no ANCOVA); B_time_handling coded 'single_timepoint' because the paper's headline primary contrast reduces to one derived baseline-to-20th-day change-score variable compared once between groups (separate from the additional baseline-to-10th-day and 10th-to-20th-day pairwise contrasts also reported in Table 3, which were not treated as the headline result). Trial registered prospectively: CTRI/2020/02/023240, registered 11/02/2020 (recruitment Feb 2020-Mar 2021, i.e., registered essentially at trial start).
